 Kamil Mishra Prioritizes Team Victory Over Personal Records
 Ratopati
 November 18, 2026
 Read in Nepali
 Kathmandu. Chitwan Rhinos batter Kamil Mishra has said that the team's victory is more important than personal records.
 After Chitwan reached the second qualifier by defeating Kathmandu Rhinos by 61 runs in the eliminator of the third edition of Nepal Premier League (NPL), he said that his goal is to take the team to the final.
Speaking at a press conference after the match, Mishra said that although the team was under pressure after losing three wickets early on, he was able to return to the game with the partnership with Ravi Bopara.
 ‘It was difficult for us when we lost three wickets in the first over. Then Ravi Bopara and I planned to stay on the crease and have a long partnership. We were successful in playing accordingly,’ he said. Mentioning that he had a good start before but could not score big, he expressed happiness at being able to utilize the opportunity he got this time.
 Mishra scored an unbeaten 120 runs in this match, setting a personal record for the NPL. This is also his first century in T-20 career. However, he said that he did not play with the goal of scoring a century. ‘The pitch was good for batting. I was thinking of fulfilling my role for the team rather than scoring a century,’ he said.
 He dedicated his first century to the Chitwan supporters, his teammates, and everyone who has supported him in his cricket journey. Speaking about the preparation for the second qualifier against Sudurpashchim Royals, Mishra said that he would focus on his own performance rather than the opposing team.
 ‘It doesn't really matter to us who the opposing team is. This is a game. If we play good cricket, we can defeat any team,’ he said. He said that although fatigue may occur due to playing for two consecutive days, he will manage it and come to the field.
 ‘Playing continuously will definitely be tiring. But it has to be managed. Chitwan has not played the NPL final yet. Therefore, our goal is to win tomorrow's match, reach the final for the first time, and make history,’ he said.
 Meanwhile, when asked whether all-rounder Sikandar Raza, who did not play in the eliminator due to injury, would play in the second qualifier, Mishra said that he is not a doctor and needs to consult the team doctor about this. He informed that Raza is in Nepal and is currently resting.
